source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Direct communication mainly to the family because the adult client's input has little value","B":"Use a single communication script for every adult with an intellectual disability","C":"Exclude support persons entirely even when the client requests their appropriate involvement","D":"Communicate directly and respectfully with the client and support autonomy as abilities allow"}}
source_row.rationale: Appropriate care for an adult client with an intellectual disability includes using clear, respectful, developmentally appropriate communication directly with the client (not solely through family/support persons), involving support persons as appropriate, and respecting the client's autonomy and right to participate in decisions about their own care to the greatest extent possible, individualized to their specific abilities.
source_row.source_detail: Person-centered care principle applied to adults with IDD: communicate directly and support participation according to abilities; accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.stem: A nurse is caring for an adult client with an intellectual disability, and a family member offers to answer all questions on the client's behalf during the visit, assuming the client's own input wouldn't add much anyway. Appropriate care instead includes:
